reviews.title: Wtf happened
reviews.text:
I used to be able to edit a video in Quik in about 10–15 minutes. Now something that should be incredibly simple has turned into one of the most frustrating editing experiences I’ve ever had.

The biggest problem is trimming clips. I trimmed a video down to 27 seconds and saved it as a new clip. My iPhone correctly shows the new video as 27 seconds. But when I bring that SAME 27-second video back into Quik to edit it, Quik somehow turns it back into approximately 53 seconds and includes footage that I already removed.

I have tried saving it as a new clip, removing and re-adding the media, and starting the edit again. Nothing fixes it.

An app designed to make quick video editing easier should not require this much troubleshooting just to use a trimmed clip. I actually like Quik when it works, which makes this even more frustrating. Please fix the trimming/editing issues because right now the app is making a simple edit unnecessarily difficult and time-consuming.

reviews.title: Great feature, very frustrating ecosystem
reviews.text:
Great feature, frustrating ecosystem

I genuinely like Quik’s automatic edits — it’s one of the main reasons I pay for GoPro Premium. But the way finished edits are handled is unnecessarily frustrating.

I can create a Quik edit on my iPhone using footage in my GoPro cloud account, but that finished video isn’t then available when I log into the same GoPro account on my Mac/web browser. To keep it in my GoPro library, I have to export it to Apple Photos, transfer/access the file on my Mac, and then manually upload it back to GoPro Cloud.

Why? I’m already paying for GoPro cloud storage. If I create and save a video in GoPro’s own app, it should simply appear in my GoPro account everywhere.

I’d also really like Quik editing back on Mac, or at least proper web-based editing. Action cameras generate huge amounts of high-resolution footage, so restricting the best editing features to a phone feels completely backwards.

Quik’s automatic editing is excellent. Please make the ecosystem around it equally good. At the moment the friction is actively encouraging me to export my footage, find another editing solution and reconsider renewing Premium (I won’t until it’s fixed) 

Or it’s hello Insta 360!

reviews.title: Adverts for premium EVERYWHERE
reviews.text:
The GoPro hardware is excellent, but the app experience leaves a very poor impression.

Immediately after setup, the app pushes a Premium subscription very aggressively. Prompts appear early and repeatedly, making it feel like a required part of using the device rather than an optional add-on. This is annoying and disappointing given the price of the camera.

To be clear, the camera works fine without subscribing, but the app’s design does not make that obvious. There is no clear, user-friendly path for those who simply want to manage their own files locally or use their own cloud storage. Instead, the experience is heavily geared towards driving subscription uptake. I did not aim to rent a camera, I bought one. 

The core functionality is there, and the camera itself is very capable. However, the constant upselling detracts from what should be a premium user experience.

I would expect:
- A clear opt-out during setup  
- Fewer subscription prompts  
- Better support for local workflows and third-party storage such as iCloud, OneDrive or Google Drive. 

This is a good product overshadowed by an overly aggressive monetisation approach. 

GoPro need to do better.

reviews.title: Does not support latest cameras
reviews.text:
I’ve owned all Hero cameras for the past decade, and the Quik app has been a very useful utility for offloading content, storing unedited originals and making edits with GPS stickers.
Auto-upload has been a welcome addition too, though I wish there was a convenient way to use it outside my home network (hotels for example).

The main reason for my 2 star review is the usability of the app since buying the new MAX2.
Metadata is not retained/applied to .360 content. This means no camera information, no location information - nothing. If you use a tool like Metapho the metadata file will be completely blank apart from the duration/resolution of the video or photo.
This means no stickers in the Quik app, and if you export content to a tool like Apple photos - no GPS tag.

I know the MAX2 is capturing GPS, as Hero mode content (single lens) does have all the metadata mentioned above - so either GoPro are falsely advertising the MAX2 as a 360 camera with GPS, or the Quik app was not updated to support .360 content properly and can’t handle the metadata.

GoPro support have been less than helpful - asking me weekly for another ‘sample video’, not acknowledging the problem. 
When competition is high as it is, I’m surprised GoPro would be willing to alienate long term customers over something so fixable.

reviews.title: GoPro removed linear transitions in 360 video
reviews.text:
My experience with GoPro is that they just simply cannot get out of their own way when it comes to destroying their own software. After waiting many months for them to restore a core feature of this app that they chose to remove I have decided I will be exiting the GoPro platform as soon as I can. I cannot believe how utterly inadequate they’ve been in failing to address this self-inflicted issue. 

I don’t know why GoPro did this but now he transitions between key frames in a 360 video default to “ease in ease out,”and there are no options to change the transition type to linear, ease in only, or ease out only. 

I submitted a support ticket on this a few months ago and haven’t heard anything back. I would be preordering the newly announced MAX2 right now if this wasn’t an issue, but as it is I will instead be removing myself from the GoPro ecosystem and going elsewhere as this is an entirely crucial component to my workflows.

How do you even mess up this bad, GoPro?
